correctness.rationale: Under identical unit chores, ex-post WEFX is equivalent to (x_i-1)/w_i <= x_j/w_j for all ordered agents, and unbiased ex-ante WEF requires E[x_i]=m*w_i. With m<n the admissible counts are zero-one and their hypersimplex admits the quota iff mw_i<=1; with m=n only all-one counts are WEFX. With m>n each x_i>=1 and y_i=x_i-1 selects the first L=m-n weighted Adams priority scores k/w_i; the scores tied at the Lth threshold form a uniform matroid base polytope and give the exact coordinate convex-hull feasibility test. Tied weights k_i/alpha and rational outside weights imply every w_i rational whenever m>=n and compatible. For rational w=a/b each score band of width b adds a_i priorities and preserves ties, proving period b of feasible counts. For two agents the integer interval (m-1)w <= x <= (m-1)w+1 gives compatibility exactly m mod b in {0,1}. Independent rational exhaustive two-agent enumeration tested all coprime denominators 2..16, m<=50; all-general proof is the priority argument.
residual_risks: Independent bounded calculations corroborate but do not prove infinite quantifiers; the reviewed mathematical proof is the universal argument.
